resultText:
The constitution is written to `.specify/memory/constitution.md` at version **1.0.0**, ratified and last amended 2026-11-10. It is the only file changed and it is not committed.

**Version rationale:** the file was still the unfilled Spec Kit template, so this is the first ratification rather than an amendment.

**How your rules map onto the template** (five principles plus two sections):

| Your section | Constitution section |
|---|---|
| Source of truth | I. Contract as Source of Truth |
| Architecture | II. Layered Architecture |
| TypeScript | III. Strict TypeScript |
| Files and style | IV. Small, Self-Describing Files |
| Tests (spec file per service, failing test first) | V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE) |
| Tests (build, lint and test must pass) | Quality Gates |
| Safety | Safety Constraints |

Every rule you supplied is carried over, reworded only into MUST / MUST NOT form.

**Assumptions I made:**
- **Tests split:** your "Tests" group is divided between Principle V and Quality Gates, because the template has five principle slots and two extra sections for your six groups.
- **Governance:** you supplied none, so I wrote the simplest set:
  - the constitution wins over any conflicting document;
  - amendments go through `/speckit-constitution` with a local commit;
  - versions follow semantic versioning;
  - every spec, plan, task list and implementation is checked against the principles.
- **Rationales:** each principle has a one-sentence rationale that I wrote; these are not from your input.
- **Ratification date:** today, as the date of first adoption.

**Checks:**
- No placeholder tokens remain and there are no TODOs or deferred items.
- No extension hooks are registered (`.specify/extensions.yml` does not exist), so none ran.
- The Sync Impact Report sits as an HTML comment at the top of the file. Spec Kit treats it as review scratch, so remove it before committing.

**Suggested commit message:** `docs: ratify constitution v1.0.0`
